steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You've decided.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Sounds like you aren't asking, Dr. Kal'tsit... Sorry, I just realized, I'm supposed to call you Lord Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: There's no point in talking about that now.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I just want to express my disappointment at your decision. You could have been a great help to Theresa.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Her Majesty... came to me alone, after the last mission.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Sounds like her.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: She said she remembered me, where I came from, in Kazdel.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: The huge industrial district, and the endless rotten, crime-ridden city of death that stretches out around it.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: The influx of refugees growing the slums up skyward.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: How many 'nobles' do you think there are in Kazdel? How many of them are Sarkaz who gave themselves some stupid title in an even stupider war?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: As many as there are weeds in a garden.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: That's a good one. They are like weeds.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: But Her Majesty might remember.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: I appreciate her kindness. She remembers the last bit of humanity left in the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: She's the only one who could.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: So why are you trying to escape?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Put it a little rougher, why don't you, Doctor?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Ines, Dr. Kal'tsit has done a lot for us. You know that.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Hmph...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: No offense intended.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If you've decided to leave, I have no right to stop you. You can go and be free, travel the world as mercenaries.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You don't need me to tell you that.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Right.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But what about the other Sarkaz?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: W has her own plans.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: And it's not like we have the power to make every mercenary follow the rules.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: That's how mercenaries are. It's a lot harder to keep order with these free spirits than with big standing armies.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But some lost Sarkaz warriors could stand to learn from you... that which you seek.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Regardless, you've chosen your path.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Even if it's a dead end.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Us mercenaries only know how to dive into war, to hide ourselves in the smoke from its wake of ruin.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...I hope that works out for you.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Thanks.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: ...There are barely any Sarkaz still following us.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: A lot of them decided to stay, but there's even more who don't get to pick where home is anymore.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: The camp's gone. The only equipment left is the bottom of the barrel stuff Babel left us.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: We're more like campers going mountain climbing than mercenaries at this point...

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: ...It's always been like that, all the way back to when we first met in that birch grove and decided to carve our own path.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Good thing Dr. Kal'tsit gave us a few special contracts. At least we'll be able to get by.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: If we're still going to be running errands for her, what difference does it make whether we leave Babel or not?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: We're just a team of mercenaries fighting to make a profit, taking a lucrative contract.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: You're lying to yourself.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: ...Wait, where's our flag?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: I kept it. And everything else. If I'm gonna lie to myself, might as well be thorough about it.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: You remember right? Back then, whenever a standard-bearer fell, another would always step up right away.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: From the west to the east, becoming a mercenary, then all the way back here. That whole time, this flag never fell.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Up until the 70th, or maybe 80th standard-bearer died. He impaled his own abdomen with the flagpole to keep it up.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: When we were escorting the Rhodes Island landship, those enemies... those monsters from Kazdel, shredded our lines like paper.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: When that happened, it was just a kid holding the flag.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: The enemy had the high ground. Arts rained down around us like a mudslide.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Before Dr. Kal'tsit arrived, there was pretty much nothing we could do to fight back.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: The flags are all in tatters.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Yes...

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: But I've still got hands. I can hold up a flagpole.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: I never liked flying a merc flag.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: It should've been stomped into the mud a long time ago.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: How many vets from the old days are still alive?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: You, and me.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: ...Let's not waste any more time.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Hey, Hoederer.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Did you leave W with Her Majesty on purpose?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: What do you think about Her Majesty? And Kal'tsit? And especially... that 'Doctor?'

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Never took you for the gossipy type.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Just making small talk.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: You didn't use your Arts once the whole time you were there. That's not like you. I was worried maybe—

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: ...I didn't have the guts. Not with the way Dr. Kal'tsit was looking at me.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: She's an unknown quantity.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Right, better not dig too deep. Just knowing who that Kal'tsit is...

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: But, I might've accidentally taken a peek at Her Majesty. My Arts can't look directly into peoples' minds. More like I can get a feel for them by looking over their 'shadows'...

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Her Majesty is very special.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: She's... tragic. But extremely resilient, and gentle.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tsit is strange. She has this almost mechanical feel to her, but like a machine, how can I put it? Full of humanity.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: ...You're talking about Kal'tsit?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: You can't feel it, can you?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: She sees us all as equals. She didn't call us 'devils.'

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Maybe just because Her Majesty was there.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: What about the one they just call 'The Doctor?'

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: ...Let's put it like this: the soldiers are the pawns in the game. The commander is the player.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: When I saw the Doctor, I was struck with the feeling that I'm always gonna be a pawn.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: That one's not a battlefield commander. The Doctor runs the whole war.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: That's not why.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Do you know what the biggest difference is between the piece and the player?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: No... But why are you talking like W now? You were always impatient. Never heard you talking in riddles like this before.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: A chess player's main focus is never on the pieces, or even the game. It's always on the other player. You always want to beat an even match.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: After a win, the player goes home to a nice, hot meal. The pieces get popped back into the box and stashed away.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: The player gets to sleep, wake up, walk, and talk.  The pieces just sit there in the cupboard.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: We're all objects. Inanimate objects. There was only one person, one thing really alive on that battlefield. And it was that one.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: If we're still gonna call ourselves people, then, well... the Doctor's something else.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Okay then. I think it's safe to say we agree on that one.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: But it looks like Her Majesty, Kal'tsit, and whoever else don't really mind.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tsit's always been careful. And even though we weren't working together for very long, I got the impression their troops are kind of in the dark about it.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: I told W: some things are already starting to change.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: ...Leaving might be the right call.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Wait, you still didn't answer my question. If we're on the same page, why'd you leave W there then?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Are you worried about her?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: So what if I am? Answer me already.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: ...For insurance. Just in case one day, we have to switch sides.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Or do you think the Regent, Her Majesty's brother, will open his heart, say 'all is forgiven,' and keep letting us raid the Lateranos?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: I want to get away from this war. I'm sick of fighting our own people... and we've already suffered enough.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: ...Hmph.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Don't get me wrong, W buying us some insurance wasn't the original plan...

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: But her face lit up when I told her she could stay...

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Tch... What an ingrate.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: You've taken to our work unexpectedly quickly.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: And that goes for your two friends as well. Though they didn't accept the Doctor's invitation to stay, they still performed their work admirably.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Uh-huh. So, did Theresa say anything?

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: ...If you seek Her Majesty's praise, you may petition for an audience with her yourself.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: Assuming that you can avoid Ms. Kal'tsit, that is.

steps.name: W
steps.text: There goes that idea. That bitch is stuck to Theresa like glue. Tch, what a headache.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Anyway, where are they now?

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: And yet you still intend to seek her out?

steps.name: W
steps.text: I just want to go take a look. Can't get chewed out for doing that, right?

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: Now who's the bigger headache?

steps.name: W
steps.text: Hey, I worked my ass off to dig out seven spies stuck in with your refugees. Seven! And a caster too! Do you know how hard that was?

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: Keep it down. Your presence, as well as the details of your mission are both confidential... Shh.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: That was your job, and if I recall correctly, the Doctor asked you to keep at least one alive.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Yeah, the 'alive' part is trickier than you'd think. Guy offed himself before I could even murk him. What's a girl supposed to do?

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: ...*Sigh*.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: They're on the bridge. Amiya should be there too.

steps.name: W
steps.text: You talk like I remember all these names. As if I care.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: That's your business...

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: ...Just a moment, what's that in your hand?

steps.name: W
steps.text: Oh, this? A little camera that I yoinked from one of the spies. Pretty rare, huh?

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: Don't tell me you're going to...

steps.name: W
steps.text: What? Is a Sarkaz gonna pass up an opportunity to get a selfie with Her Majesty?

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: ...Well, if Ms. Kal'tsit apprehends you as a spy, don't expect me to bail you out.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Sure, sure.

steps.name: W
steps.text: How'd those spies manage to get in here anyway?

steps.name: W
steps.text: Don't you think... we've been going at our fights kinda weird lately?

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: That's not an area where you or I should be pointing fingers. If you're dissatisfied, take it up with the Doctor.

steps.name: W
steps.text: The Doctor, huh?

steps.name: W
steps.text: Maybe next time then.

steps.name: W
steps.text: (Over there? Sure enough, of that's all of them. I'm gonna lie low for a sec.)

steps.name: W
steps.text: (What's with the tiny bunny? The little shit's ears are blocking Theresa!)

steps.name: W
steps.text: (Uh oh! Kal'tsit...)

steps.name: W
steps.text: (...She's not coming over here? Did she not see me?)

steps.name: W
steps.text: (Damnit, what's the Doctor doing here? Get that one in my picture and it's 100% cursed...)

steps.name: W
steps.text: (Aww, Theresa's laughing.)

steps.name: W
steps.text: (Screw it, I won't get another opportunity like this!)

steps.name: W
steps.text: Cheese—!
...W, do you even know what's going on right now?
Uhh, probably better than you do? I'm the one actually down on the battlefield putting in work, 'Dr. K'~
It's fine, Kal'tsit. There's no need to be angry—

steps.name: W
steps.text: Ugh, what a bitch... All that over a stupid picture!

steps.name: W
steps.text: But you might not like the next job so much, Mr. Captive.

steps.name: Sarkaz Captive
steps.text: Mmmf! Nnnngh...!

steps.name: W
steps.text: C'mon, don't be so nervous. You brave enough to get so close to the Speaker's Office. Surely you came prepared to have your cover blown?

steps.name: W
steps.text: And I'm in a pretty bad mood, so you're not gonna have a good time.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Hm? Trying to off yourself?

steps.name: W
steps.text: Don't rush it. We're not ready for that. Not until I ask you some questions first. Now what was it...?

steps.name: W
steps.text: What happened at the Battle of the Mill last month?

steps.name: W
steps.text: What reason do you have to be here? Why are you so close to the capital?

steps.name: W
steps.text: What are you after? Who do you answer to? What were you trying to give Theresis?

steps.name: W
steps.text: Oh, take your time, no need to knee-jerk me an answer here.

steps.name: W
steps.text: What I really want to know is, say there's an Originium needle hovering by that eye you can't close. If I was to slowly push it in at a speed of three millimeters per second—

steps.name: W
steps.text: Would you be afraid?
Hoederer's prediction was correct. The war is starting to change.
But to be honest, I lost interest in watching the situation in Kazdel unfold... Not like it affects me, anyway.
I'm just worried... about Theresa.
Even though seeing that damned woman is about as revolting as seeing my reflection smiling back at me in the mirror, maybe I do have to talk to her.
She and I are the same kind of person. If she can even be considered a 'person,' that is. That's one of a whole bunch of mysteries floating around her.
But she's much stronger than me. Maybe she will be able to protect Theresa—
No, she has to.
Otherwise—–
